items.quote: The calorimeter consists of a thick aluminium cylinder containing two small electric furnaces, which are used for starting the reaction in the sample and for electric calibration, respectively.

The alloys which were synthesised directly in the high temperature reaction calorimeter were prepared starting from pellets of the mixed powders weighing about 0.7 g sealed in tantalum crucible under an argon atmosphere and were dropped from a room temperature thermostat (300 K) into the high temperature calorimeter.

items.calibration: dropping four silver spheres of known weight, two before and two after the alloy
items.quote: In each run, the calorimeter was calibrated with a procedure consisting in dropping four silver spheres of known weight, two before and two after the alloy.

The DSC111 SETARAM apparatus designed as a Calvet calorimeter (where the cylindrical reference and working cells are surrounded by two differentially connected thermal fluxmeters) was used by continuous heating mode to perform enthalpimetric analysis on xNi 1⁄4 0:50 and 0.55 samples.
Measurements were carried out under flowing argon and using alumina crucibles, after proper calibration with tin and indium standards.
A power compensation Perkin Elmer DSC7 equipment was used in order to determine melting enthalpies on xNi 1⁄4 0:22; 0.33 and 0.55 alloys.

items.method: X-ray powder diffraction, optical and electron microscopy and electron probe microanalysis
items.quote: All the samples were analysed by X-ray powder diffraction, optical and electron microscopy and electron probe microanalysis in order to check their equilibrium state.
The alloys were prepared from elements with purity of 99.9 mass% (Ce) and 99.99 mass% (Ni) by arc melting or direct synthesis in the calorimeters.
items.synthesis: arc melting or direct synthesis in the calorimeters

items.quote: Samples to be used as 'reference' against those prepared in the calorimeter and those for DSC measurements, were obtained by either induction melting of stoichiometric amounts of the constituent in gas-tight tantalum crucibles sealed by arcwelding under argon or by arc melting under an atmosphere of Ar gettered with Ti.
items.synthesis: induction melting of stoichiometric amounts of the constituent in gas-tight tantalum crucibles sealed by arcwelding under argon or by arc melting under an atmosphere of Ar gettered with Ti

items.calibration: melting temperatures of Al (660.32   C), Ag (961.78   C), Au (1064.18   C) and Ni (1455.15   C)
items.quote: DTA apparatus (DSC404C, NETZSCH, Germany) was used to measure the phase transition temperatures. The sample holder material was pure Al2O3, and solid samples with weights of about 50e100 mg were taken from the annealed samples. The measurements were performed between room temperature and 1450   C with a heating and cooling rates of 5   C/min in an argon atmosphere. The temperature was measured with PtePt/ Rh thermocouples and calibrated to the melting temperatures of Al (660.32   C), Ag (961.78   C), Au (1064.18   C) and Ni (1455.15   C). In the temperature range examined, the accuracy of the temperature measurement was estimated to be  2   C.
